articleTitle: Price and Quote Index Prediction with Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: Estimating the values of stock indices, financial instruments, or cryptocurrencies is a complex task due to the involvement of economic, social, and political factors that are generally unpredictable or unquantifiable. The commonly used methodologies for this task include heteroscedastic models such as ARCH and GARCH, which predict volatility or the intensity of price changes through returns, allowing for short-term predictions of up to 1, 3, or 5 days, or even longer. Recently, Machine Learning models have shown promising results in this field. This research explores the use of Deep Learning techniques by constructing an artificial neural network of the Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) or Feed-Forward type to approximate the value of the Mexican Stock Exchange Index, which measures the performance of the Mexican stock market. A comparison of these models was made using standard metrics such as Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), concluding that the MLP provides improved results. However, the limitations of the proposed learning method highlight the need for alternative models in stock index prediction, and the Power Law model is suggested as one such alternative.

articleTitle: De'Nu: Design of a Mobile Application for Learning the Cuicatec Language
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: This document presents the design of a mobile application for learning the indigenous Cuicatec language, named De'Nu, targeted at students of a university. The design process was guided by the user-centered methodology. During the testing phase, three iterations were conducted to evaluate the prototype's usability through specific tasks, resulting in an average evaluation score of 8.8. Participants successfully completed the tasks, highlighting the speed and efficiency of the system. The results indicate a positive reception from users, who expressed satisfaction and interest in the implementation of Augmented Reality technology for learning indigenous languages. Overall, the application was effectively designed and easy to use, providing a unique experience for users.

articleTitle: Using a Niko-Niko Calendar with ARCS to Improve the Team Members' Motivation in Software Projects
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: This paper presents an agile approach to track the team members' emotional state in software projects by using the Niko-Niko Calendar. The calendar encourages open communication, empathy, and continuous improvement for enhancing team dynamics and fostering a positive work environment. Since the original calendar proposal does not include a guideline on how the emotions shared by the team members could be handled, this paper suggests the usage of the Attention, Relevance, Confidence and Satisfaction Model to provide motivational feedback. The proposal was implemented in a project of one software enterprise in Mexico, obtaining a positive evaluation from the practitioners who responded a questionnaire based on the Instructional Materials Motivation Survey.

articleTitle: A Fuzzy Cognitive Map to Evaluate a Medical Context
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: A fuzzy cognitive map is a graph that allows the representation of knowledge. Particularly, it focuses on systems where uncertainty exists. Fuzzy cognitive maps have been applied in medicine, notably for medical diagnosis. In contrast, this paper presents a case study focused on a medical context, where we evaluate the progress of the interactions between a patient, a multidisciplinary doctor's team, and the activities involved in the patient's recovery. In the rehabilitation process, there are uncertainties when monitoring the treatment established by the medical team, so we use computer-assisted collaborative work (CSCW) to help in measuring the interactions. In this sense, nowadays, doctors do not follow a method to record the patient's medical activities per the treatment plan. Therefore, in this work, we propose a fuzzy cognitive map to monitor and evaluate the activities involved in comprehensive stroke rehabilitation.

articleTitle: Design of a Mobile Application for the Dissemination of Tourist Attractions Using the Design Thinking Methodology
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: This paper describes the process of designing a mobile application for the dissemination of tourist attractions in the community of Villa de Tamazulapam del Progreso using the Design Thinking methodology, in the first stage (empathy) interviews were carried out with some tourists to know their needs and with this an empathy map was developed, later in the definition stage, The requirements of the software were established by identifying the user stories, in the idea phase. In the first stage (empathy) interviews were conducted with 25 tourists, to know their needs and develop an empathy map; in the definition stage, the requirements of the software were established defining the user stories; in the idea phase, brainstorming was developed to indicate the elements that the application should include, subsequently, a high-fidelity prototype was designed and evaluated considering the usability metrics: effectiveness, efficiency and satisfaction, Throughout the process, feedback was obtained from users.

articleTitle: A Reasoning System for Graded Modal Logic
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a deduction system for the modal logic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{K}$</tex> with graded modalities, which is obtained by adding numerical constraints to the modal operators. Graded modalities can be seen as a generalization of traditional modal operators since they include numerical bounds in the modalities, thus enabling the formal treatment of more detailed expressions, such as “there are at least <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n+1$</tex> individuals satisfying a certain property”, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> is a natural number. This kind of properties commonly arise in contexts such as concurrent systems: “if at least 3 processors are free, then proceed to compute the next task”, or epistemic logic:”if more than 2 people know <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex>, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex> is known”. The system is based on the notion of tree-hypersequents. We show the system is correct, i.e. sound and complete.

articleTitle: Transforming Semi-Structured Data into Structured Data by Using R
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: The increasing use of digital platforms has boosted the generation of databases with heterogeneous data. So, Model Driven Engineering faces the challenge of developing efficient methodologies that deal with semi-structured data for their treatment and analysis. This paper applies the R language to develop a transformation chain that links models with different abstraction levels. Such a transformation also transforms semi-structured data into structured data, which allows us to facilitate the analysis of heterogeneous databases. In this sense, we show that the R language can be applied to solve software engineering problems since <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex> provides an environment that guarantees maintainability, reusability, and extensibility concerning the treatment of heterogeneous databases.

articleTitle: Data Visualization to Support Diabetes Management: Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: The complexity of diabetes-related data requires its conversion into intuitive graphical representations, making it easier to identify patterns, trends, and correlations crucial to understanding patient conditions. These visualizations improve understanding of the disease and enable healthcare professionals to make more informed and personalized decisions. In addition, empowering patients to interpret their data fosters greater control over their diabetes management, which can improve health outcomes and quality of life. Visualizations play an essential role in research, allowing researchers to identify areas of interest and knowledge gaps and guiding future research to improve care. However, a problem with using complex visualizations in diabetes monitoring systems has been identified, prompting a systematic literature review to examine their role in disease management. The findings of this review include examples of systems that encourage patients' active participation in their self-care, as well as the use of IoT devices to enhance the effectiveness of graphical visualizations. The study also discusses the methodology used, a summary of the results, and challenges and opportunities, highlighting the importance of data visualizations in diabetes management.

articleTitle: Design of a Digital Navigation Assistant in EMINUS for People with Visual Disabilities
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: Requirements analysis is crucial in software system development. With the growth of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based solutions, this analysis has gained greater importance to create more robust and accessibility-focused solutions. This study defines the software requirements for designing a virtual assistant that utilizes Natural Language Processing (NLP) to facilitate navigation through voice commands for visually impaired people on the EMINUS educational platform, belonging to the Universidad Veracruzana. The necessary requirements are detailed using Google Cloud Text-to-Speech API, neural networks with Bayesian classification algorithms, Rest API services through Node.js, JavaScript, and HTML5 for creating a plugin in Google Chrome.

articleTitle: Influence of the Entry Profile for the Software Engineering Bachelor Degree on a Successful Academic Trajectory: Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: Various studies that evaluate and predict dropout in universities have been published. However, few refer to the relationship between the entry profile and a successful academic trajectory. In software engineering (SE), the entry profile constitutes mathematical logical reasoning and thinking as well as problem-solving skills. However, there are other factors such as social and economic, parents' education, number of failed subjects, admission exam results among others that can influence school performance. In this research, we use machine learning algorithms to evaluate the entry profile of students in the software engineering program at the University and relate it to a successful academic trajectory or dropping out of the program. Using a collection of 306 SE students from the 2014, 2015, 2016, and 2017 cohorts, and 33 variables obtained from their electronic records, correlation analysis, stepwise regression, multinomial logistic regression and decision trees were performed. It was found that to have a successful academic trajectory in SE program, the student should be under 19 years old, have no failed subjects in high school, and have an overall score between 81 and 85 points on the admission exam. Those who did not complete their academic trajectory had at least one remedial exam in high school.

articleTitle: Search-Based Software Testing Driven by Bioinspired Algorithms: A Systematic Literature Mapping
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: Bioinspired algorithms have gained relevance in Search-Based Software Testing (SBST) mainly because they can find multiple solutions to difficult-to-solve problems. Exploring the usage trends and elements of its implementation is necessary for software engineering since it allows for understanding the area's current state and proposing guidelines for innovation. We proposed a Systematic Literature Mapping to analyze the canonical bioinspired algorithms used in SBST. During the mapping conduction, 60 studies were analyzed, in which bio-inspired algorithms were used in different software testing activities, such as test data generation, test case generation, test case prioritization, and others. The practical implications of our research are significant. The most commonly applied bioinspired algorithms in these activities are the Genetic Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization, and Ant Colony Optimization. Concerning problem types, most of these algorithms are focused on single-objective, with or without constraints, and, to a lesser extent, multi-objective and phased problems. According to the results, SBST driven by bio-inspired algorithms favors variables such as execution time and computational cost. Code coverage is usually used as a performance metric to evaluate its effectiveness. The application of canonical bioinspired algorithms mainly seeks to solve single-objective problems.

articleTitle: Gender Diversity in Software Development Teams: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: In recent years, social aspects, including gender diversity, have gained increasing prominence in various fields, including software engineering. Gender diversity has emerged as a significant area of interest within the industry; however, its impact on development teamwork environments remains subject to mixed perceptions among team members. We conducted an examination of gender diversity in development teams, focusing on member collaboration and team performance. Through a systematic literature review encompassing 30 studies from the last five years, we explored the advantages and challenges faced by development teams when incorporating gender diversity into their work environment. The findings of our review suggest that gender diversity promotes greater cohesion within teams and contributes to a more conducive work environment. Moreover, it enhances critical aspects such as innovation, creativity, and product quality, ultimately boosting team performance. However, gender-diverse profiles encounter unique barriers that hinder their retention within the industry. These barriers include a lack of opportunities to assume key roles, gender discrimination, biases, and insufficient recognition of their contributions. Our study highlights the multifaceted nature of gender diversity in development teams, underscoring both its positive impacts and the challenges that need to be addressed to fully leverage its potential in the software engineering domain.

articleTitle: User Modeling Using EEG Signals: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) has emerged as a critical tool for user modeling in brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), offering unique perspectives into cognitive processes and user behavior. This systematic review explores how EEG signals have been used to model various facets of user behavior, from attention and cognitive load to emotional responses and personality. We analyze transdisciplinary studies incorporating EEG in BCIs, This review highlights advanced signal processing techniques. Additionally, it examines machine learning algorithms that enable sophisticated interpretation of brain signals in real-time. In addition, we observe how these method-ologies are applied in contexts ranging from collaborative gaming to device control in home and clinical settings. Through the integration of key findings, this review identifies trends in the accurate modeling of user behavior and performance of BCIs, as well as the challenges inherent in working with interindividual variability and neurophysiological signals.

articleTitle: Enhancing Emotional and Performance Data Collection for Agile Software Engineers: A Continuous Strategy Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: Agile Software Development (ASD) has become the industry standard, facilitating rapid delivery of high-quality software by prioritizing flexible, iterative processes and the interactions of agile software engineers over rigid procedures. Hence, the performance assessment of agile software engineers should consider their emotions. In this study, we aim to take the first steps toward implementing a strategy for collecting affective and performance data using biometric devices and project tracking tools through a mixed-methods study. First, we analyzed interviews on emotions and performance metrics among local agile software engineers. Second, we conducted a quantitative analysis using emotional data tools and a project tracking tool (Jira) with software engineering students on a local company project. Results indicated (i) the most experienced emotions of agile software engineers, (ii) the most used metrics to assess their performance, (iii) the discrepancy between self-assessments and biometric measurements, and (iv) the relationship between stress, emotions, and task progression in projects. Future research should aim to enhance emotional data collection strategies to reduce complexity and improve response rates, providing better insights into the emotions-performance dynamic in agile environments.

articleTitle: Enhancing Visibility of Components and Dependencies Across Diverse IT Environments with Open-Source Software-Bill-of-Materials Generation Tools
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: This paper explores the escalating adoption of Open-Source Software (OSS) and its implications on traditional software assets inventory practices. While OSS offers undeniable benefits in terms of flexibility and cost, it also introduces complexities, especially in managing intricate dependency structures within the software supply chain. In response to this, the concept of Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) is proposed as a potential solution, aiming to bring transparency by documenting software components and dependencies. This paper presents an empirical study that evaluates the effectiveness and efficiency of a set of SBOM generation tools across diverse IT infrastructures and software inventory tools. It highlights SBOM's tools advantages, such as discovering OSS components installed without reliance on OS package managers, and providing component dependencies' information. By addressing this, we aim to deepen the understanding of SBOM's significance in modern software management practices and provide insights for optimizing SBOM generation tools usage.

articleTitle: Human-Computer Interaction behind the EEG Signals of ADHD People: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: The analysis of the electroencephalogram (EEG) signals within the Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) field is a helpful method when it comes to reducing the bias that usually arises while obtaining data for evaluating information interactive systems. The needs of a group of people with specific characteristics can be unveiled by the interpretation and comparison of their interaction responses, as well as in a more objective way, throughout their EEG signals. Particularly, this strategy is not a common practice during the execution of research for the development of new technologies directed at Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) people. The present work is a systematic literature review (SLR) about how EEG signals have been implemented to identify or differentiate people with ADHD within the fields of computer science and engineering. Hence it aims to provide a wide scope related to the advancements in the area of HCI intended for the above-mentioned population. Together with classifying the associated recent contributions to identify different opportunity areas that remain unexplored. This review was executed by following the methodology proposed by Kitchenham, through which 20 articles were selected as final primary studies. The performed analysis allowed the identification of relevant applications, along with potential research areas.

articleTitle: Towards a Systematic Refactoring Method to Support Deployability
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: This article presents a systematic refactoring methodology to support deployability, applicable to any type of application, with the goal of improving or incorporating the quality attribute of deployability. We focus on applications that did not consider this attribute during the early stages of design. The methodology consists of four stages: Evaluation, Analysis and Prioritization of activities, Refactoring, and Re-evaluation, which together allow for continuous improvement of the deployment process each time they are applied. To test this methodology, we worked with three different development teams where the initial stages were applied. Additionally, a prototype was built in which all four stages were implemented, successfully proving the methodology's effectiveness and achieving optimal results that improved the deployment process of the prototype.

articleTitle: Transforming Software Complexity Analysis with the ECB Metric
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: This paper introduces the Extended CB (ECB) metric, a novel approach in software complexity analysis that addresses limitations in traditional metrics. The ECB metric extends the CB metric by incorporating additional cognitive complexity factors, such as compound expressions and try-catch blocks, providing a more comprehensive assessment of software complexity. This inclusion is a significant innovation, as it offers a nuanced understanding of the cognitive challenges involved in modern software development. The detailed comparative analysis between the CB and ECB metrics highlights the technical improvements and the higher complexity values reported by the ECB metric. These higher values accurately reflect the true cognitive load required for code comprehension and maintenance, leading to practical applications in project estimation, resource allocation, and quality assurance. The ECB metric is also valuable for educational tools, enhancing novice programmers' learning experiences. The potential impact of this research is substantial, promoting better software design, maintainability, and overall quality. Future research could further refine the ECB metric and expand its applicability across different programming paradigms and environments, broadening its utility and impact.

articleTitle: Secure Cryptography Usage in Software Development: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: Cryptography plays a significant role in software engineering, its application is paramount for the security of software systems. However, comprehending and securely utilizing cryptography in software development is complicated and prone to error. To mitigate these challenges, it is crucial to know best practices and utilize appropriate tools to aid in the implementation of secure and accurate cryptography in software projects. Unfortunately, this insightful guidance is frequently fragmented to developers and software engineering students seeking to integrate these principles into their projects. With this problem in mind, we conducted a Systematic Literature Review, yielding 52 primary studies. The review uncovered a range of essential tools, including cryptographic APIs, Integrated Development Environments, and static anal-ysis tools, designed to identify vulnerabilities in the initial phases of software development. Furthermore, we emphasized the importance of implementing effective strategies, such as regularly updating libraries and selecting appropriate cryp-tographic algorithms. On the contrary, we also underscored detrimental practices, such as utilizing outdated functions and depending on unreliable sources like online forums. Many studies mention that tools are being developed and tested for elementary or high school students to start learning basic cybersecurity topics, including cryptography. There is also a trend for developers to use these tools to mitigate vulnerabilities in software developments, highlighting the importance of this topic.

articleTitle: Towards a Learning Analytics Model in Higher Education Applied to a LMS in Virtual Education Based on Motivation Indicators for Permanence
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: In recent years, the impact of Learning Analytics applied to higher education through HEIs has been identified in order to understand the academic performance of students, based on the interaction that students have in an LMS, using descriptive analytics, for example. However, there are few works that have focused on the integration of information from various sources, in addition to considering motivation as a fundamental part of student permanence in an academic course implemented in an LMS. This paper presents a proposed model of learning analytics in higher education applied to an LMS in virtual education based on motivation indicators for permanence. A review is presented of the way in which motivation has been measured in previous works and the model for carrying out said measurement in the future is proposed, by extracting the data generated through the use of an LMS. An analysis of the traditional measurement of motivation is presented, where two specific instruments are implemented such as AMS (Academic Motivation Scale) and IMI (Intrinsic Motivation Inventory), suggested by the reviewed literature, in addition to identifying the indicators that will be considered in the measurement proposal. The data of the Instituto Tecnológlco Superior de Perote is taken as a case study. It is a first version of the proposal and work is still being done on its development and implementation. As results, a first analysis of the data is presented applying unsupervised machine learning techniques used for predictive analytics.

articleTitle: Methods for Evaluating the User Experience of Applications for Deaf Users: A Mapping Review
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: As a part of the software development life cycle, it is important to understand both the expectations and perceptions of each individual. This is not only to ensure functional software but also to make it more enjoyable. This process is part of the discovery phase associated with the concept of user experience (UX). Therefore, it is crucial to carry out UX evaluation tests to determine if the generated products really meet people's needs. On the other hand, emphasizing accessible design, it involves addressing aspects related to the equivalent user experience but for people with disabilities, in a similar way offering positive and even accessible experiences when interacting with a system. The objective of this mapping review is to provide an overview of the application of UX evaluation methods and their adaptation for application to users who are hard of hearing or deaf. We conducted an evidence map of publications based on the definition of research questions, keywords, the definition of information sources, eligibility criteria and a search strategy. The data were then synthesized and categorized. As a result, 12 publications met the eligibility criteria. It was found 13 UX evaluation methods suggested for application with Deaf people; of which 77% of the instruments were tested with Deaf users while the remaining 23% were not. Among the adaptations identified, the inclusion of Sign Language, the use of simple scales and ensuring that the instruments do not depend on verbal information stand out.

articleTitle: Agent-Based Modeling and Simulation for Collaborative Software: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: In the design of collaborative software in a traditional way, it is often overlooked how complex user interactions become in a social context. This article presents a systematic literature review, investigating the most recent work in simulation and agent-based modeling (ABM), with a focus on group interactions, to support collaborative software. This review explores how ABM can close this gap by simulating group dynamics and social interactions. We analyzed the reviewed studies to identify how ABM can be used to model user interactions within collaborative software environments, design socially intelligent software agents, and understand user psychology within social networks. Using research results from ABM simulations that model the psychological principles of users, or incorporating data from social networks, for example, software engineers can develop collaborative software that integrates seamlessly with human social behavior. This approach has the potential to lead to the development of more user-friendly, efficient and socially intelligent software systems.

articleTitle: Exploring LLM Tools Through the Eyes of Industry Experts and Novice Programmers
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: At present, Large Language Models (LLM) and Generative AI models have emerged and impacted industry and society. LLMs are Artificial intelligence (AI) systems designed to understand and generate human language. The rise in popu-1arity of LLM-based systems has motivated research into their use in education, including code generation tools, automated feedback systems, and support for student software projects. The release of ChatGPT™ marked a significant milestone, providing an accessible tool for IA interaction. ChatGPT™ has gained popularity among students, not only in software areas. This study analyzes the perspectives of software engineering students and software engineers on using LLM tools such as ChatGPT™ for software development projects. In this study, we use a questionnaire to analyze different viewpoints and graphics to show the experiment results between these groups. The findings of this study are expected to provide valuable contributions to the understanding of how LLM tools are perceived in the context of software development and their potential implications for educational practices and industry standards.

articleTitle: A Novel Framework for AI-Integrated Electronic Manifest Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)

authors.preferredName: María Teresa De Jesus Chew Lee

abstract: In logistics and other sectors, automation is revolutionizing our daily lives. This paper explores the field of automation in the trade of international goods: the chance to reduce errors and inefficiencies in generating the formal electronic manifest, an essential legal document for all transported goods, through state-of-the-art artificial intelligence (AI) techniques include natural language processing and machine learning for data extraction and workflow optimization, as well as image analysis models for improved product description generation. A model to improve the quality of product descriptions with image-based automated captioning and measured the performance of the model to generate the electronic manifest is presented. It was tested with a natural language processing and machine learning toolkit called BLIP, which is based on the popular supervised translation model. A model for image captioning, to improve the product description via an API. The main result of this reported work is that AI-powered solutions are likely to reduce human effort in performing many tasks for generating an electronic manifest, decrease human error rates, and expedite processing times.

articleTitle: Cluster Analysis in the Identification of Patterns in Software Development with Agile Methodologies: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: Software Engineering is a discipline that aims to deliver quality software products. To this end, several development methodologies have been proposed, with agile methodologies being the most recently used, which promote the continuous delivery of functional software in short cycles called iterations or sprints. In these deliveries, there are activities where the identification of patterns in different software arti-facts is necessary. An example of this is the detection of similar artifacts to avoid redundancy or reuse artifacts. This study presents a systematic review of the literature that seeks to analyze the activities, development stages, benefits, and challenges that have been reported when applying various cluster analysis algorithms to identify patterns in agile methodologies. Fifteen primary studies selected through the Kitchenham methodology were analyzed. It was observed that k-means, k-medoids, and hierarchical clustering are the most used approaches in various stages of development such as requirements, design, and testing. Furthermore, the most analyzed artifacts were user stories. Finally, the studies reveal various advantages, such as pattern identification without a priori knowledge, variance reduction, and development time reduction, among others. However, the parameterization of these algorithms is still a fundamental challenge to be addressed in future work.

articleTitle: Empirical Research on Secure Development in Agile Methods: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: Although agile methods and secure software development often operate under different principles, the need to integrate both approaches has gained attention due to growing security concerns in software development. As a result, there has been an increase in empirical research in this area. This study aims to analyze the current state of empirical research on secure development within agile methods, focusing on the empirical methods applied, the challenges, and the findings. A systematic literature review was conducted, selecting 33 studies through defined inclusion and exclusion criteria, followed by identifying the trends and patterns in the collected data. The selected studies highlight various empirical methods used to evaluate the integration of security practices in agile environments. Common challenges were identified, providing a comprehensive view of the areas needing development.

articleTitle: Agile User-Centered Development of Mobile Applications: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: Given their nature, mobile applications require a high degree of usability, thus necessitating development processes which procure this quality attribute. Among such processes are those which integrate agile software development (ASD) with user-centered design (UCD), whose efficiency in creating more usable software has been proven in non-mobile software development projects. This study presents a systematic literature review with the aim of identifying the state of the art of agile-UCD Integration applied to mobile application development. A total of 32 studies were included, leading to the synthesis of frameworks used to integrate ASD with UCD, the UCD techniques involved in the process, the software tools used to design apps under agile-UCD, the challenges in adopting this approach as well as recommendations for their mitigation, and the benefits that both developers and users of mobile apps obtain when their software is developed with this approach.

articleTitle: Detecting Pass-the-Hash Attack in a Microsoft Active Directory Environment using an Open-Source Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: The pervasiveness of Pass-the-Hash (PtH) attacks within Microsoft Active Directory environments poses a high security risk to organizations globally. This paper proposes an open-source based system for detecting PtH attacks. We systematically dissect the attack vector, which capitalizes on the vulnerability inherent in the Windows New Technology LAN Manager authentication protocol. The paper highlights the steps that attackers would use to conduct the PtH attack including acquiring the hash through system exploitation or credential theft, using the hash for impersonation without requiring the plaintext password, and achieving lateral movement to escalate privileges within the network. Furthermore, it outlines the discreet nature of PtH attacks that evade traditional security measures, emphasizing the significance of a robust and layered defense strategy. Our results demonstrate that it is possible to leverage these affordable technologies to improve the detection of malicious activities in an organisation's network, improving its security posture.

articleTitle: Transforming Software Development: A Study on the Integration of Multi-Agent Systems and Large Language Models for Automatic Code Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: This paper explores the integration of Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) and Large Language Models (LLMs) for auto-matic code generation, addressing the limitations of traditional manual coding. By conducting a comprehensive review of existing literature and analyzing a practical case study, we demonstrate how MAS and LLMs can collaboratively enhance software development processes. The research focuses on the technical and theoretical challenges of this integration, highlighting the potential for improved productivity, adaptability, and quality in code generation. The findings contribute to AI-based software engineering by revealing new research directions in collective intelligence and automated programming.

articleTitle: Social Software Engineering: Developing Interactive Video Games to Support Educational Lag in Rural Communities of Baja California Sur, Mexico
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: Educational lag is a social issue exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly in rural communities. Addressing this challenge requires innovative approaches, especially the use of educational technologies and interdisciplinary collaboration. This paper presents a case study in which students from the Universidad Autónoma de Baja California Sur (UABCS) developed a set of educational video games as part of an integrative interdisciplinary project, involving students from Software Development Engineering and Education Sciences programs. Using the Social Software Engineering (SSE) approach, the project focused on creating digital tools that are relevant to the local educational context of a rural middle school, in collaboration with Escuela Secundaria Técnica No.8. The project not only provided a comprehensive educational experience for university students but also aimed to mitigate the educational lag in rural areas. The paper discusses the theoretical background, including the importance of SSE, integrative projects in higher education, the impact of educational technologies on rural communities, and university social responsibility. The methodology outlines the stages of video game development and highlights the importance of user participation in ensuring cultural and contextual relevance. The results demonstrate the potential of these educational games to enhance learning experiences, while the discussion addresses the limitations, including the need for objective, long-term assessments. Future work involves evaluating the usability of these games in real classroom settings, facilitated by teachers, and an ongoing collaboration agreement that will allow the games to evolve based on educational outcomes and feedback. This study underscores the crucial role of universities in promoting educational equity and social responsibility through the development of tailored technological solutions.

articleTitle: Analysis of Natural Language Processing Techniques and Tools for Requirements Elicitation: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: Requirements Engineering (RE) encompasses ac-tivities such as requirements elicitation, analysis, specification, and validation, which are essential in software development for defining and aligning stakeholder needs and expectations. However, these processes are often laborious and prone to errors and misunderstandings, resulting in systems that fail to meet expectations and require costly revisions. This study specifically focuses on requirements elicitation, as accurate and comprehensive gathering of requirements is vital for the success of subsequent activities. The aim is to explore how Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques and tools can enhance requirements elicitation, emphasizing their adapt-ability to diverse linguistic contexts. A Systematic Literature Review (SLR) identified the most commonly used Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques in NLP, such as Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and Transformer-based approaches like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT). The Natural Language Toolkit (NLTK) is recognized as a prominent tool in the broader NLP domain, while the ELICitation Aid (ELICA) tool stands out for its application in requirement elicitation. Despite the advantages offered by these approaches, it is crucial to acknowledge and address their limitations. Further research is recommended to enhance their effectiveness, particularly in adapting to languages other than English.

articleTitle: State of the Art of the Security of Code Generated by LLMs: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: AI -assisted programming has experienced a surge in popularity over the past few years, largely thanks to advancements in Large Language Model technologies. This has led to the emergence of tools like ChatGPT and GitHub Copilot. However, the use of AI models for code generation comes with a downside: the resulting code is susceptible to vulnerabilities, thus posing new challenges in the field of secure software development. In this study, we analyze the current state of research regarding the security of LLM generated code from the Software Engineering perspective. We conducted a Systematic Literature Review following the guidelines from Kitchenham et al. The search process included five sources: IEEE Xplore, ACM, Science Direct, Springer Link and Wiley Online Library. We also included an iteration of backward and forward snowballing. We obtained 3104 peer-reviewed studies though Quasi-Gold aided automated search and selected the most relevant ones through 5 stages. The final selection includes 15 primary studies from which we extracted and synthesized data. We identified seven different kinds of security vulnerability present in LLM generated code, six different mitigation strategies and practices, and four tools recommended by authors to use in conjunction with LLM code generation. Security related issues within LLM generated code have only just begun to be explored, initial research has already emphasized the significance of considering the inclusion of AI-powered code generation in software projects, as it carries the risk of introducing vulnerabilities at a higher rate than human-generated code. The vulnerabilities, practices and tools identified in this study, can potentially help developers to use LLM programming assistants more responsibly, making informed decisions when leveraging LLM technology.

articleTitle: Identification of Practices for Representing Indigenous Groups in Software Requirements Elicitation: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: Software engineering is a discipline that impacts everyone throughout society. However, sometimes end users are not considered in the requirements elicitation process, leading to their needs being ignored and resulting in systems that may not be used. Furthermore, when the users are indige-nous groups, their beliefs, traditions, or lack of technological resources can lead to the rejection of the software. This paper analyzes the documented information in the literature that compiles practices focused on the representation of indigenous groups in software requirement elicitation through a systematic literature review. Twenty-six primary studies from four digital libraries were analyzed, identifying various techniques and approaches used to address the characteristics of these groups in the elicitation process. It is concluded that one of the most appropriate ways to elicit and understand the needs of indigenous groups is through direct observation and the inclusion of these groups in development, thus promoting their interests within the reported case studies. Also, challenges such as limited understanding of cultures, the difficulty in identifying the customs and beliefs of the communities, and intergenerational gaps were identified.

articleTitle: User Story Automation in Software Engineering: Insights from the Literature
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: User stories are widely regarded as an effective method for articulating software requirements, especially within agile development. However, the brevity often encouraged in user stories can lead to a lack of detail, resulting in miscommunication and inefficiencies during development. A significant challenge is the manual extraction of user stories from unstructured text, which is labor-intensive and prone to errors. Automated extraction using Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Machine Learning offers a promising solution. These technologies can identify and extract user roles, actions, and benefits from unstructured text, reducing the reliance on manual intervention and ensuring consistent quality. We conducted a literature review spanning the past 20 years, from 2004 to 2024, on which we identified 77 relevant articles, with only 10 focusing on the extraction of user stories using NLP techniques. These studies emphasize the need for automation in user story extraction to improve the efficiency and accuracy of requirements gathering. The findings highlight a gap in current research regarding automated extraction methods and the importance of addressing this through advanced NLP techniques. Implementing such solutions can transform the handling of user stories, making the requirements elicitation process more efficient and less error-prone, ultimately contributing to the success of agile software development projects.

articleTitle: System-Oriented Testing on the Microservices Architecture: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: The Microservice Architecture (MSA) is gaining popularity in the industry and literature as a raising research topic. This architectural style brings advantages such as independent development, testing, and deployment. However, it is also plagued with many challenges due to its distributed nature. In the case of testing, complex dependencies, heterogeneous execution environments, and independent development teams make it difficult to test microservices using traditional methods and techniques. Our goal is to provide a collection of tests, tools, state-of-the-art solution proposals, as well as relevant challenges. To achieve this, we conducted a Systematic Literature Review following the guidelines presented by Kitchenham. We searched through search engines including IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, and Wiley Online Library. In total, we retrieved 13,556 articles and thoroughly analyzed them. Through this process, we identified 44 primary studies that were suitable for data extraction and synthesis. From our analysis, we identified 12 testing strategies that are applicable to the MSA. Additionally, we found proposed solutions for automated testing along with microservices benchmarks. Furthermore, we discovered a set of testing tools and challenges specifically related to MSA-based system testing. The main challenges we encountered include automated testing, performance testing, and finding realistic MSA-based systems. Our study aims to benefit software engineering practitioners and researchers interested in microservices testing by providing a comprehensive understanding of the current landscape of testing for MSA-based systems.

articleTitle: Helen: An Intelligent Virtual Assistant for People with Auditory Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence has grown exponentially to improve human interaction with the world. The most common examples are virtual assistants such as Alexa, Siri, Cortana, or Google, and electronic devices that can connect with other electronic devices in the home. Undoubtedly, incorporating these virtual assistants and devices has supported and improved the interaction of users with low technological experience or people with a motor impairment who can also benefit from them. However, people with auditory problems who are commonly limited verbally and use sign language to communicate can not use virtual assistants in their current design. Therefore, some authors have pointed out the importance of developing devices and creating environments so that people with auditory disability can improve their interaction with these devices. Hence, this study aims to introduce Helen, a virtual assistant for people with auditory disability. Its design is based on a qualitative analysis of semi-structured interviews with people with auditory problems. Helen can perform some actions using sign language. This study presents the results of the interviews, the details of Helen's design, the hardware construction, and the user interface design. We firmly believe this project will serve as a cornerstone for empowering the deaf community, providing them with a virtual assistant to control various home devices.

articleTitle: Identifying Key Factors for Using Ethnography in Software Requirements Elicitation: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: During the early activities of developing the require-ments for a software product, selecting appropriate elicitation techniques is crucial. If not addressed early, missing, misin-terpreted, and incorrect requirements can lead to significant rework. The selection process for the elicitation techniques involves thorough analysis to determine if the chosen techniques are suitable for the product and project. Ethnography could be used as a requirements elicitation technique; although it is not commonly utilized, it has proven useful under certain circumstances. The main objective of this research is to identify case studies where ethnography has been employed as a requirements elicitation technique and to identify common features among them. A systematic literature review is conducted to achieve this objective, utilizing automatic searching across five different databases. This search yielded eleven studies where ethnography was used as an elicitation technique. Our findings determined that ethnography is particularly beneficial in five types of projects: collaborative projects, critical system projects, inter-field projects, high-budget projects, and projects where the analyst lacks domain expertise.

articleTitle: A Fresh Perspective on Measuring Complexity in Object-Oriented Software
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: The measurement of software complexity is a critical component in the development of modern software systems, directly influencing maintainability, scalability, and reliability. As software projects grow in complexity and scale, the need for effective complexity management becomes increasingly vital. This paper contributes to the body of knowledge by introducing the Aggregated Weighted Complexity (AWC) metric, a novel and comprehensive tool designed to evaluate software complexity in object-oriented programming. The AWC metric is significant in that it integrates multiple dimensions of complexity-structural, data, control, systemic, and cognitive-thereby offering a holistic assessment that addresses the multifaceted nature of software systems. The potential impact of the AWC metric is substantial. By offering a detailed and actionable measure of complexity, the metric helps in reducing technical debt, improving code quality, and fostering sustainable development practices. It encourages the adoption of best practices in concurrency management, exception handling, and memory management, all of which are crucial for developing reliable and efficient software systems. Future research will focus on empirically validating the AWC metric across diverse programming languages and development frameworks. Additionally, there is significant potential for integrating advanced technologies such as artificial intelligence and machine learning to enhance the metric's predictive capabilities. Expanding the applicability of the AWC metric to include emerging programming paradigms will further broaden its utility and relevance, ensuring it remains a vital tool for complexity management in modern software engineering.

articleTitle: Systematic Literature Review of Low-Code and Its Future Trends
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: With the growing demand for software, it is necessary to look for new approaches that allow faster de-liveries, without compromising the quality of the final product. Among these new approaches to development is low-code, which emerged as a proposal for applications development, minimizing the need for manual coding. Its application is associated with the use of low-code development platforms (LCDPs), a term most commonly used when discussing low-code in general. This work presents the results obtained from a Systematic Literature Review (SLR), which sought to understand the current state and future trends of the low-code approach to be considered by software engineers as an alternative to high-level programming languages. Applying knowledge of Software Engineering would take care of the quality of the process and the product. This would allow the decrease of time and costs in the construction of software. Fol-lowing Kitchenham's methodology, the characteristics, benefits, challenges and trends of low-code were identified. Although low-code has gained significant ground, there is a notable gap in comprehensive SLRs focused exclusively on this approach, as it is often discussed in conjunction with the no-code approach. After examining various databases such as IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, ScienceDirect, and SpringerLink, fifteen rele-vant primary studies (published between 2018 and 2023) were selected. Among the findings, it was discovered that the characteristics of LCDPs include to use graphical interfaces, support for external services, collaborative development and reuse. The benefits encompass rapid development, cost reduction, ease of use and strong integration. However, challenges such as lack of customization and scalability are faced. Future trends include adoption by small and medium sized enterprises (SMEs), integration with DevOps, and digitalization efforts. Careful evaluation is recommended for effective implementation of low-code approach.

articleTitle: A Website for Mexican Sign Language: A Usability Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: Mexican Sign Language (LSM) has facilitated communication between deaf and hearing individuals; however, studying this language can present challenges due to its visual format. While books exist that represent signs on paper, there is no better learning method than when the sign is recorded on video and the movement and joints can be seen in three dimensions. Online video repositories exist to search for signs or phrases; however, this information is disjointed or specialized sites on these topics have very few videos. In both cases, searching for signs and learning LSM becomes complicated. To address this situation, a Collaborative Web System is proposed that allows searching for sign videos based on text inputs. In this way, research supports people in establishing communication with deaf people. In addition, the site is collaborative since deaf and hearing people can collaborate by adding their knowledge about LSM. The experiment consisted of developing a usability and interface test. The results show that the system is considered to have adequate usability aspects, however, with other points for improvement. This proposal allows the development of a social application to facilitate the study and learning of Mexican Sign Language, as well as to transmit knowledge of this language, which favors LSM communication.

articleTitle: Digital Assistant to Improve User Experience on Websites: Innovative Support and Efficient Communication Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: The integration proposal of an innovative chatbot into the Yachay system highlights its current status as an internal project, yet to be fully integrated into the educational framework. Within Yachay Tech, the initiative named “Intelligent Systems for Personalization and Flexibilization” signifies a proactive leap towards improving the quality and accessibility of higher education in Latin America. At the core of the Yachay website lies a pioneering chatbot strategically poised to debut and revolutionize virtual education. Drawing insights from user satisfaction studies and subsequent design iterations, the proposal aims to enhance crucial metrics such as adaptability, user experience, and personalized engagement. While the chatbot's potential benefits remain to be validated against real-world outcomes, the methodology section meticulously outlines its implementation process. This includes developing logic, integrating with Yachay databases, ensuring interactivity, managing exceptions, and conducting trial implementations. Adapted assets from diverse countries within the Yachay project collaborated seamlessly to ensure integration success. Digital assistants envisioned as pivotal components within the Yachay project are set to drive qualitative and quantitative advancements in the educational landscape. Despite the chatbot's current proposal stage, its potential to revolutionize virtual education is evident, offering a glimpse into a future where adaptability, engagement, and innovation converge to redefine the educational experience. It's noteworthy that internal tests preceded the testing phase with various user types. These tests involved diverse phrases and words, assessing metrics like response time, which averaged a swift 2.1 seconds. These internal evaluations are crucial steps towards implementing the proposal effectively within the system for users.

articleTitle: Next-Generation Metric for Software Complexity Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference in Software Engineering Research and Innovation (CONISOFT)
abstract: This research introduces the Holistic Cognitive Complexity (HCC) metric, an innovative object-oriented measurement method evolved from the traditional CB metric to offer a more comprehensive assessment of software complexity. By integrating additional complexity factors such as array usage and thread management, the HCC metric addresses both structural and cognitive complexities, providing a holistic view of modern software development. The practical utility of the HCC metric is demonstrated through a comparative analysis with the traditional CB metric, using a sample program to highlight the added intricacies captured by the HCC metric. The detailed complexity assessment facilitated by the HCC metric enables developers to identify potential problem areas early in the development process, guiding targeted refactoring and optimization efforts. This proactive identification of complexity hotspots is crucial for maintaining high standards of software quality and ensuring maintainability and scalability over time. Additionally, the HCC metric aids in better resource allocation and project planning by providing a more accurate measure of complexity, thus supporting effective project estimation and resource distribution. The significant contributions of the HCC metric include its ability to quantify the complexities introduced by advanced programming constructs like arrays and threads, offering deeper insights into software complexity than traditional metrics. This research underscores the importance of continuous enhancement of complexity metrics to address emerging challenges in software development. The HCC metric's robust framework and detailed assessment promise to elevate software quality, reliability, and maintainability, making it a valuable tool for software developers, analysts, and project managers.
